stem: ____ is valuable in science, even when a scientific idea is true, it can be misused through grandiosity.
She knew well, from experience with hundreds of hired crew members on her boats, how (i)____ attitudes can be: one negative influence can impel an otherwise (ii)____ member of a crew to quit.

Thinking (i)____ about one’s choices can sometimes (ii)____ decision making. For example, in one study in which college students selected their favorite poster from a set, those asked to explain their selection ended up less (iii)____ their choices than those who were not asked. Researchers concluded that thinking of reasons interferes with people’s ability to access gut-level reactions that are crucial to sound decision making.

A decisive way to test planet formation hypotheses is to study planetesimals, but these objects are quite ____, neither numerous nor large enough to emit significant radiation that can be captured by telescopes.

The ____ of native South American textiles at the time of the Spanish conquest should not be surprising: it represented the apogee of one of the world's oldest and most sophisticated weaving and dyeing traditions.
If it is wrong to justify human selfishness on the basis of the alleged selfishness of nature, then it is equally mistaken to espouse ____ merely because some animals happily assist each other.

In many branches of science, our knowledge and technology have advanced so rapidly that new studies carried out with improved instruments and techniques may well ____ research done just twenty years earlier.
